schema:name: Differentiated/stratified contribution structures implemented and repeatable
schema:description:
A mature structural outcome achieved when a health system successfully deploys and consistently maintains an income-indexed, progressive fee or tax architecture for health financing. This operational milestone replaces flat-rate or regressive premium models with automated, bracketed contribution tiers that scale dynamically based on a citizen's socioeconomic status, corporate revenue, or employment sector, embedding these rules directly into the state's payroll and tax enforcement systems so they execute reliably year after year.

Its primary purpose is to institutionalize financial equity and risk-pooling across the health economy. By ensuring that wealthier individuals and highly profitable enterprises shoulder a proportionately larger share of the funding base while low-income, informal-sector, or vulnerable populations receive deep subsidies or full exemptions, this repeatable mechanism prevents catastrophic out-of-pocket health costs from driving citizens into poverty and secures a socially just, predictable revenue stream.

Example: A national social health insurance agency fully implements a differentiated contribution structure that automatically syncs with the central revenue authority; salaried workers in the top tax bracket are accurately assessed a 4% monthly health contribution, middle-income workers pay a flat 1.5%, and informal laborers or citizens below the poverty line are auto-enrolled with a 100% state subsidy—with the entire bracket system recalculating seamlessly at the start of every fiscal year.
